$schema_note: The map's drawn decisions, in the words they were asked for. Every row is either enforced by a rule this suite runs (test/app/lib/map-decisions.mjs) or pending with the question that blocks it. A decision that is not in this file is a decision nothing stops from reverting — which is the whole reason the file exists. Checked twice: test/app/map-decisions.test.mjs against the style module, and functional.mjs against the style a real browser is drawing.

rules.area-layers-are-shapes: Every World layer whose truth geometry is an area is painted as a fill. `covers` must account for every polygon layer in WORLD_LAYERS that is not named in a pending row — so a new area layer added later is covered on the day it lands, not the day someone remembers.
rules.min-line-width: A line layer is at least this many pixels wide at this zoom.
rules.line-weight-order: Line layers ranked heaviest first, asserted on the widths the style actually ships.
rules.paint-order: [under, over] — the second layer is painted after the first.
rules.has-casing: The layer ships a `-case` layer beneath it, wider than its own stroke.
rules.smooth-bends: Every way is drawn with round caps and round joins. A mitred join spikes where a walkway turns and a butt cap leaves a square end at every segment break, which is what makes a curved midway read as a run of straight sticks.
rules.area-edge-drawn-as-outline: A layer that draws only an outline is allowed exactly when the area it outlines is itself painted as a shape, below it. `shapeBeneath` names that fill.
rules.drawn-at-every-zoom: The layer is in no LOD hide-group, so nothing ever toggles it off — and its paint is quiet at the wide end: thinner than the midway and under full opacity, so being always-drawn does not become clutter.

decisions.asked: walkways and broad areas use shapes and smooth bends
decisions.why: A parking lot outlined is a lot you read as a fence. Broad ground — the lot, the lake, the lawn, the building footprint — is an area in truth, so it is an area on the map, and the outline is the shape's edge rather than the whole of it.

decisions.asked: roller coasters displayed more visual and thicker on the map
decisions.why: Coaster track is the thing the park is famous for and the landmark a guest navigates by. Drawn at 1.6px it sat lighter than the midway it flies over and read as a stray scribble. Asserted at ride scale (z16), which is where track carries full weight — at park-wide it is deliberately the lighter line, and `coaster-visible-at-park-wide` holds that end. The order is the whole World tier's line weight, so making track heavier by thinning the midway does not satisfy it. `boundary` is out of this chain — it is the park edge, held by its own row.

decisions.asked: roller coasters displayed more visual and thicker on the map
decisions.why: Heaviest-of-the-lines is a ranking, and a ranking survives everything shrinking together. This is the floor, and it is set at the zoom the track first appears: `worldLod.js` hides the coaster layer below 0.7 px/m, which at this latitude is about MapLibre zoom 15.5, so a floor asserted at a wider camera would be pinning a width nothing draws. Six pixels at the moment track becomes visible, ramping to ten as a single ride fills the screen.
Track passes over the station house, the midway and the lot in life. Painted under any of them the ride is chopped into pieces wherever the park is busiest.

decisions.asked: paths read as walkways, not as gaps in the grass
decisions.why: One wide line in the ground colour under the path. Without it a midway crossing a lawn has no edge and reads as a gap in the grass.

decisions.asked: walkways and broad areas use shapes and smooth bends
decisions.why: A midway is a curve, and MapLibre's default join is a mitre: every bend in it spikes and every segment break ends square, which is what turns a drawn walkway into a run of straight sticks. Round caps and joins are the whole of what makes a way read as one continuous shape.

decisions.asked: walkways and broad areas use shapes and smooth bends
decisions.why: A walkway a guest is meant to follow with a phone at arm's length is a shape with width, not a hairline. Paired with the casing below it, that width is what gives the midway an edge against the lawn.

decisions.asked: walkways and broad areas use shapes and smooth bends
decisions.why: `boundary` is the one area layer drawn as a line, and it is allowed to be: it is the edge of the `park` fill directly beneath it, and it sits above every ground layer, so filling it would paint over the lake. The rule holds it to that — take the park fill away and the boundary becomes a bare outline, and this fails.

decisions.asked: make coasters visible at park-wide zoom without making the map too visually complicated
decisions.why: The view the app opens on is the whole park, and a coaster park with no coasters in that view is the plainest possible failure of "displayed more visual" — thickness cannot fix a layer that is not drawn. worldLod.js used to hide track below 0.7 px/m, so no width would ever have shown there. It is drawn at every zoom now. The second half of the ask is the constraint: a hairline under full opacity, lighter than the midway, so at park-wide it reads as a landmark you can find the ride by rather than as the line spaghetti ADR-0012 warns against. Both halves are asserted, because either one alone is the wrong map.
